Badminton.title: 'Importance of finding...': Virat Kohli’s one piece of advice helped PV Sindhu end her longest title drought and win a BWF Super 750 title in Japan Open
Badminton.summary: 'Importance of finding...': Virat Kohli’s one piece of advice helped PV Sindhu end her longest title drought and win a BWF Super 750 title in Japan Open The Economic Times
Badminton.body:
The 31-year-old shuttler won her maiden BWF Super 750 title at the Japan Open after defeating three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi of Japan in straight games in the women's singles final in Tokyo on Sunday. The triumph marked Sindhu's biggest title since her historic BWF World Championships victory in 2019. Before this, her recent titles included the 2022 Singapore Open Super 500 and the 2024 Syed Modi International Super 300.

With the Japan Open win, Sindhu became the first Indian shuttler to claim the prestigious title and ended a title drought of more than two years. Sindhu's journey to the Japan Open crown was far from easy. The previous two years were among the toughest periods of her career. A stress fracture interrupted her progress, while her Paris Olympics campaign ended with an early exit.Repeated injuries and rehabilitation challenges made her comeback difficult. With every setback, the pressure surrounding one of India's most celebrated athletes continued to grow. However, Sindhu found a new perspective during a conversation with Virat Kohli, who himself has experienced the pressure of performing at the highest level.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Another Peak for Popov
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Another Peak for Popov BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Christo Popov delivered a near-flawless performance to claim the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026 to earn a morale-boosting title win ahead of the BWF World Championships next month. Koki Watanabe had had a draining three-game match against Yushi Tanaka in the semifinals, but to his credit, the home hope didn’t make it easy for the Frenchman, particularly in the second game. Watanabe had his chances in the second, but Popov’s greater sharpness and ability to last the rallies helped him nudge the tape, 21-11 21-19, for his third title of the year.

“This means a lot… it’s confirmation of what I was talking about for the last few months or weeks,” said Popov. “For me, it’s a very big achievement. Most of all, I like to play in Japan. I’m very happy to bring the title this year.

Badminton.title: PV Sindhu scripts history, becomes first Indian to win BWF Japan Open
Badminton.summary: PV Sindhu scripts history, becomes first Indian to win BWF Japan Open WION
Badminton.body:
Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu delivered a throwback performance, defeating Akane Yamaguchi in straight games and capturing her maiden Super 750 title at the Japan Open on Sunday. She became the first Indian to win the tournament, sealing a 21-17, 21-17 victory over the three-time world champion and ending a title drought of more than two years. It also marked her biggest triumph since the World Championships crown in 2019, with her previous title coming at the Syed Modi International in 2024.

Yamaguchi, playing her sixth Japan Open final, had enjoyed the upper hand in recent meetings, Sindhu had not beaten her in a completed match in four years, with their last full-match win dating back to the Thailand Open in 2022. Their earlier clash at the Malaysia Open this year ended prematurely after Yamaguchi retired following the opening game.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Kong Makes Triumphant Return After Surgery
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Kong Makes Triumphant Return After Surgery BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Kong Hee Yong’s return to competitive badminton following a right knee surgery culminated in a dream title, with the women’s doubles final among the most dramatic in recent times.

Kong was out of action after the Badminton Asia Team Championships in February for the knee surgery and rehab; the world No.8 making a return with Kim Hye Jeong only at the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026. The high point of the return was in the final game against Jia Yi Fan/Zhang Shu Xian, which went the Koreans’ way, 14-21 21-15 30-29. The see-sawing final game saw either side have six match points before Zhang Shu Xian blew a kill just wide, and the Koreans collapsing in a flood of emotions.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Pusarla Breaks Title Drought
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Pusarla Breaks Title Drought BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
It has been four years since Pusarla V Sindhu won a title at the upper end of the HSBC BWF World Tour. Her last Super 500 title was over four years ago — the Singapore Open in May 2022. And while there were Super 300 titles and the Commonwealth Games gold in 2022, her last major title had come seven years ago, at the BWF World Championships 2019.

The relief and joy at breaking this pattern was written all over her face as she revelled in the feeling of winning the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026; the Super 750 triumph marking a high point in her career, and putting her back in the conversation as a contender at the upcoming BWF World Championships.

Badminton.body:
BWF World Championships to kick-off, organisers on Saturday promised a trouble-free tournament after last year's India Open was marred by pigeon droppings, a monkey intrusion, dust and facility concerns. TOI has learnt that cost-effective hybrid shuttlecocks will also be used, amid soaring feather shuttle prices.

Badminton Association of India (BAI) general secretary Sanjay Mishra said the shortcomings exposed during the India Open have been comprehensively addressed ahead of the Aug 17-23 event, which is expected to cost the federation anywhere between Rs 15-20 crore to host.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Yamaguchi Leads Home Surge
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Yamaguchi Leads Home Surge BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Once Akane Yamaguchi had staged a surreal comeback, there was no looking back for Japan. The home fans’ reigning deity, nearly down and out against Kim Ga Eun, broke her opponent’s heart as she completed her 11th straight victory over the Korean.

What followed was a dream day for Japan, with Yushi Tanaka upstaging No.2 seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn to enter his maiden Super 750 semifinal, Koki Watanabe taking down third seed Anders Antonsen, and Kodai Naraoka prevailing in a 98-minute marathon against Alwi Farhan.

Badminton.title: Rising star Dalvi reaches BWF Italian International quarter-finals
Badminton.summary: Rising star Dalvi reaches BWF Italian International quarter-finals Luton Today
Badminton.body:
Luton badminton star Nadeem Dalvi has taken another significant step towards his dream of representing England on the biggest stages after an outstanding performance at the BWF Italian International in Bolzano recently.

The 21-year-old battled his way from the qualifying rounds to reach the quarter-finals of the prestigious international tournament, producing a string of impressive victories against experienced opponents from around the globe. His run of successes included triumphs over India’s Koushik Dinesh Mudlukoplu and Suveer Pradhan before defeating Shashwat Dalal in straight games, underlining his ability to compete with players from one of badminton’s strongest nations.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026: Chirag Shetty says focus is on World Championships and Asian Games
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026: Chirag Shetty says focus is on World Championships and Asian Games Telangana Today
Badminton.body:
India's men's doubles star Chirag Shetty says he and partner Satwiksairaj Rankireddy are focused on peaking for the BWF World Championships and the Asian Games. The duo will also look to defend their historic men's doubles gold at the 2026 Asian Games.

New Delhi: India’s star doubles shuttler Chirag Shetty says he and long-time partner Satwiksairaj Rankireddy are fully focused on making the most of two of the biggest events on the badminton calendar this year, the BWF World Championships and the Asian Games.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Malaysians Spring Surprise
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Malaysians Spring Surprise BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Just five tournaments into their partnership, Jimmy Wong and Cheng Su Yin knocked out in-form pair Mathias Christiansen and Alexandra Boje on their way to a first semifinal. It was Christiansen and Boje’s earliest defeat since the All England in March, after which they had embarked on a brilliant run which saw them win four titles from five finals.

Wong and Cheng, whose partnership started at the Malaysia Masters where they ran into the Danes, turned it around today with a calm performance, disallowing the Danes any substantial opening.

Badminton.title: Lakshya Sen leads India's hopes as Shi Yu Qi, Kunlavut & Popov among top international stars to light up
Badminton.summary: Lakshya Sen leads India's hopes as Shi Yu Qi, Kunlavut & Popov among top international stars to light up The Times of India
Badminton.body:
BWF World Championships returns to India after 17 years, the spotlight will firmly be on a star-studded men's singles field. Scheduled from Aug 17–23 at the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium here, the tournament will feature some of badminton's biggest names alongside the sport's next generation of stars. Here are five players who have all the ingredients to leave their mark on the championships. TOI takes a look...

The reigning world champion and current World No. 1, Shi Yu Qi heads to New Delhi as one of the biggest favourites for the title. Widely regarded as one of the most complete players on the circuit, the Chinese star is known for his deceptive stroke play, tactical intelligence and ability to dictate rallies. After finishing runner-up at the 2018 World Championships, Shi completed his redemption story by winning his maiden world title in 2025. With multiple Super 1000 titles and Thomas Cup triumphs to his name, the 30-year-old will be eager to defend his crown on Indian soil.

Competitor News.title: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership
Competitor News.summary: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership Wholesale Manager
Competitor News.body:
Ritter Sport UK is accelerating its expansion across the convenience channel through a new permanent wholesale partnership with Parfetts, bringing five of its bestselling block chocolate flavours to all nine depots nationwide from this month.

The move forms part of Ritter Sport’s wider strategy to significantly grow its presence within the UK’s 50,000-strong convenience sector, making the brand more accessible to shoppers wherever they choose to buy chocolate. By increasing physical availability across convenience and independent retail, Ritter Sport aims to recruit new shoppers, build brand awareness and drive long-term category growth.

Competitor News.title: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership
Competitor News.summary: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership Talking Retail
Competitor News.body:
Rum Raisin & Hazelnut, Marzipan, Milk Whole Hazelnut, Dark Whole Hazelnut and Pistachio will now be available to Parfetts’ network of 1,950 Go Local stores and more than 6,000 independent retailers, giving retailers access to one of the UK’s fastest-growing block chocolate brands while offering shoppers greater choice through premium-quality chocolate and distinctive flavour innovation.

The new permanent listing gives independent retailers the opportunity to differentiate their confectionery fixture with a brand that continues to outperform the wider market. At a time when consumers are eating less chocolate but demanding far more from every bite, Ritter Sport believes convenience retailers are well placed to capitalise on growing demand for products that deliver genuine quality, flavour and value.
